newsitem.title: FRANCE: International human rights group slams Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: International human rights group slams Vietnam.

text.p: A Paris-based international human rights groups on Friday described communist Vietnam as a place where workers were exploited, and corruption and prostitution were rife and being controlled by officials.

The scathing indictment of the left-leaning International Federation of Human Rights (FIDH) painted a picture of a society virtually identical to that of the former South Vietnam which collapsed in 1975.

The FIDH said drug use was rife, especially among youths, and child prostitution, a common phenomenom under the fallen pro-American administrations of yesteryear, had resumed and was often controlled by the military or Communist Party officials.
The group said the Vietnamese government openly recognised its failings in the fight against corruption.

It recalled clashes between some rural populations and authorities, including a recent case where police shot villagers resisting the takeover of their ricefields intended to be transformed into golf courses for visiting foreign businessmen.
The condemnation was contained in a long apppeal to heads of state invited to a summit of French-speaking states in Hanoi in November.
The FIDH asked them to demand that Vietnam release political and religious prisoners and allow press and trades union freedom.

The statement said Vietnam's attempts at modernising its economy had resulted in sweatshops where workers were paid pitance wages for long hours, there was no security, and sexual harassement of women was common.

The FIDH statement followed Vietnam's first formal statement on internal troubles, made on Thursday by a foreign ministry spokesman who said authorities in northern Thai Binh province were taking steps to restore order there following reports of some of the country's worst unrest in years.
He said officials had been disciplined over the matter and provincial authorities were working to bring matters under control.
